title: Minimax Precision for Exponential-Tilt Causal Contrasts under Band-Limited Dose Measurement Error
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision pass and all cited leaves verified, but paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < field floor 7.4 caps achieved tier at incremental; fixed-channel finite-certificate frontier has no bounded same-topic lift.
gap_reasons: The delivered match concerns the explicitly specified finite-certificate sequence; the analytic bounds leave the diverging root-n penalty between a logarithmic power and a substantially larger subpolynomial envelope. The framing reserves the elementary equivalent for oeq:all-order, so that unresolved sharpening does not invalidate the finite-sequence match.
Certificate totality supplies an exhaustive terminating search, but no runtime bound, implemented certified solver, or reproducible active primal/dual calculations establish its practical usefulness.
The results concern one fixed known channel and bounded Lipschitz model, with no demonstrated application or extension to the cited dietary-exposure classes.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a matched finite-certificate risk and honest-length frontier for one fixed band-limited dose-error model, with near-parametric analytic bounds and a diverging root-n penalty. Mathematics, decision logic and all six citations passed D0.5, but the projected paper score 6.2 was below the field threshold 7.4, yielding incremental tier. The elementary all-order equivalent remains open; formalization was not started and no Lean module was produced.
tldr: A fixed band-limited dose-error channel identifies an exponential-tilt causal contrast while deleting an open region of frequencies. The proved precision theorem equates minimax absolute error and globally honest connected-interval length to the explicitly evaluable finite-certificate sequence \(r_n=h_n\), uniformly for integers \(n\ge1\). The finite-certificate transfer is proved in the original binary marked iid experiment, with unknown natural dose density: weighted likelihood geometry, observable dual scores, legal alternatives and positive clipped normalization connect the numerical sequence to both decision criteria. The proved analytic bounds establish \(r_n=n^{-1/2+o(1)}\) and \(\sqrt n r_n\to\infty\), ruling out uniform root-sample-size precision under those criteria. Among the mathematical rate questions, only the elementary all-order equivalent remains open. This is a specialization to the displayed fixed model, with limited class-inclusion transfer of its lower bounds; it does not extend any cited published model class.
gap: Generic convex recovery and functional-risk duality already relate scalar estimation to testing difficulty \cite{JuditskyNemirovski2009ConvexProgramming,PolyanskiyWu2026,JuditskyNemirovski2020Fractional}. Scalar density-functional deconvolution uses globally nonvanishing transforms \cite{Pensky2017LinearFunctionals,ButuceaComte2009}; zero-aware density risk treats isolated zeros \cite{BelomestnyGoldenshluger2021GeneralDeconvolution}; ordinary-smooth EIV regression has asymptotic curve bands \cite{KatoSasaki2019EIVBands}. These results do not evaluate the stipulated open-frequency-gap channel for a binary marked, unknown-density nonlinear exponential-tilt contrast and its finite-sample globally honest connected-interval length frontier. Continuation identification alone does not quantify attainable precision.
fill: The focal object is the terminating finite numerical sequence \(r_n=h_n\), with original-record attainable procedures and all-procedure converses. Every approximation is budgeted at \(n^{-1/2}\). The finite transfer joins the weighted marked likelihood, observable dual scores, legal alternatives and nonlinear normalization. The remaining analytic question concerns a closed elementary equivalent, rather than an assumed leading exponent. General convex duality, continuation identification and the homogeneous-response reduction are established tools.
